title: CO2 Laser-Assisted Deep Sclerectomy Surgery Compared with Trabeculectomy in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: Two-Year Results

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

indication: primary open-angle glaucoma with medically uncontrolled IOP, no previous intraocular surgery, adults (retrospective comparative, two surgeons; 77 eyes of 62 patients)

groups.description: CO2 laser-assisted deep sclerectomy (IOPtiMate) with mitomycin C under the conjunctiva and scleral flap; preoperative laser iridoplasty/iridotomy for narrow angles at the site, postoperative pilocarpine for 3 months, laser goniopuncture or iridoplasty for peripheral anterior synechiae as routine care
superior trabeculectomy with mitomycin C under a half-thickness scleral flap, sclerostomy and peripheral iridectomy

exclusions.what: Table 3 columns C9-C14 of R5 (repeated-measures ANOVA F and P)
exclusions.reason: test statistics and p-values are not admissible
duplicate of the Table 3 preoperative cells, which are cited instead
success proportions and Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

exclusions.what: Results text IOP before/after laser goniopuncture, iridoplasty or needling in subsets of eyes
exclusions.reason: subsets defined by a postoperative event; not tabulated series

notes: Study procedure is 'other' because the two arms are in different contexts; each group declares its own procedure (CLASS = nonpenetrating; trabeculectomy with MMC = trabeculectomy).
Roles: two established procedures compared retrospectively, neither declared experimental, so both are control groups.
Reference kind: inclusion required medically uncontrolled IOP and patients used several medications preoperatively (Table 1, Table 3 R8-R9); no washout is described.

Additional glaucoma surgery (GATT in some CLASS eyes, trabeculectomy with or without cataract surgery in some Trab eyes) and bleb needling occurred during follow-up; the article does not state that these eyes were removed from the visit means, so no outcome-defined exclusion applies.
The Results text and Table 3 disagree in the last decimal place for the CLASS 24-month mean; the Table 3 cell is cited.
Some patients contributed both eyes (77 eyes, 62 patients).
Mean number of medications per visit is tabulated in Table 3 R8-R9 (not extracted).

series.notes: cells 'value ± value' without a stated statistic; the Results text describes them as mean IOP; columns Preoperation, after 1 wk, 1, 3, 6, 12, 24 mo; per-visit n not reported (one eye lost after 3 months)
